summary: Number of paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m x n grid moving only right or down.
mainInsight: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j] + dp[i][j - 1], with the first row and column equal to 1; it can be rolled to one row. Combinatorially, any path has m - 1 downs and n - 1 rights, so the count is C(m + n - 2, m - 1).

approaches.name: Recursion
approaches.summary: paths(i, j) = paths(i - 1, j) + paths(i, j - 1).

approaches.name: DP table / rolling row
approaches.summary: Each cell sums the cell above and to the left.

commonMistakes: Initialising the first row and column with 0
Swapping m and n when sizing the table

promptVariants: What recurrence counts the paths in a grid with right and down moves?
cards.explanation: A cell is reached from above or from the left.

promptVariants: How does the combinatorial formula follow from the problem?
cards.answer: Every path consists of exactly (m - 1) downs and (n - 1) rights in some order, so the number of paths is the number of ways to choose which of the m + n - 2 moves are downs: C(m + n - 2, m - 1).
keyPoints: Choose the positions of the downs
cards.explanation: Compute with multiplication and division in a loop to avoid huge factorials.
One DP cell per grid cell (O(min(m, n)) with the formula).

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: A single row of the table (O(1) with the formula).

promptVariants: How many paths are there in a 1 x n or m x 1 grid?
options: 1: there is only one straight line of moves
n: any cell of the line may be skipped on the way
2: you can go right or down at the first cell
0: the grid has no interior cells to walk through
cards.answer: 1: there is only one straight line of moves
cards.explanation: The first row and column all have a count of 1.

incorrectOptionExplanations.2: you can go right or down at the first: In one row only right moves exist.
